scope: Control, configuration and published monitoring for DAPHNE (one shared 1 Gb Ethernet link per board; HD and VD), Light Calibration Module and PDS PoF laser boxes. Data readout and optical timing transport excluded.
author_design_decisions: One board CCM Ethernet connection through switch to physical server; retain daphne-icd SFP baseline
FD-VD: 1344 channels / 32 channels per board = 42 boards; FD-HD: 6000 / 40 = 150 boards

DAQ CCM requests run-variable and local timing-endpoint configuration through the component integrated into the SC-provided external OPC UA server; Hermes receives configuration on its separate IPBus/UDP endpoint; it does not publish counters
Configuration and control use request/response; all monitoring is published

daphne-server publishes firmware counters, timing state and applied readout configuration through the OPC UA server to DAQ opmon; SC monitors voltages, temperatures, fans, readout link diagnostics including SFP I2C monitoring, service status and versions; SC and opmon subscribe independently to their respective monitoring data through the OPC UA bridge

Timing configuration and monitoring use two paths: GbE exposes the local controls defined by the daphne-os endpoint service, including reset and endpoint address, plus endpoint status and timing-SFP I2C status; DTS optical fibre carries the remaining timing configuration and monitoring such as alignment status. Endpoint reset precedes DTS configuration. Both DAQ and SC access these controls and GbE monitoring through OPC UA; configuration/control uses request/response and monitoring is published. Delivery of DTS readiness evidence to SC remains to be specified.
SC publishes board readiness from current board-generated timing and recovery evidence

Only the protocol architecture diagram is retained; no detailed variable inventory or optical transport/readout specification. The timing section identifies the split GbE/DTS configuration and monitoring paths.
Use DUNE-DAQ/daphne-os for daphne-server, Protobuf schemas, endpoint recovery documentation and runtime services.
Include the Light Calibration Module and PDS PoF laser boxes in scope, physical/service placement and protocol requirements.

PDS provides photon detector and light calibration hardware, firmware, native services, detector specifications and detector operating restrictions. SC provides control/monitoring infrastructure and arbitrates access to detector controls and monitoring data. DPS provides protection infrastructure and detector protection. DAQ is a user of the detector.

Section 2 is Physical interface; Section 3 is Protocols and services. Each contains separate DAPHNE, Light Calibration Module and PDS PoF laser box subsections. Each hardware system has its own service-location table and protocol description.
Use Light Calibration Module (LCM) throughout. State the control/monitoring inventory for LCMs and PoF laser boxes within their respective physical-interface subsections.

LCMs use the same timing protocol and split configuration/monitoring paths as DAPHNE. Both DAQ and SC access local endpoint configuration and GbE monitoring through the LCM service/OPC UA adapter; the same acknowledgement, arbitration, access during timing outages and readiness requirements apply.
PoF interacts with SC and DPS only. It has no DAQ client, availability subscription or other DAQ interface.
The summary explicitly includes Detector Protection System interfaces and its protection infrastructure and detector protection role.
Use EDMS ID 3309688, matching the draft, as instructed by the author.

SC assesses and publishes detector status and availability. DAQ shall check the published status and take data only when SC advertises availability; DAQ configures the detector, collects detector data and provides calibration datasets agreed in advance with PDS. Ops handshake ownership remains open.

PoF uses a compact PLC and OPC UA integration with Ignition. PLC-to-OPC-UA protocol, driver, transport, ports and server placement remain undecided. Do not assert a separate PoF native service or an adapter hosted on an SC physical server.

PDS shall provide monitoring information sufficient for SC to assess and confirm detector health and diagnose readout network connections, including SFP I2C diagnostics. This responsibility covers service and firmware status, firmware and service versions, OS health, detector health and readout link diagnostics; the document describes categories and does not enumerate individual variables.

DAPHNE service placement: AXI / OS -> daphne-server -> ZMQ on DAPHNE; ZMQ client -> OPC UA bridge on the SC bridge server; OPC UA client -> Ignition on the SC server. AXI and OS are both inputs to daphne-server. DAQ configuration and arbitration remain in the OPC UA bridge; Hermes stays separate.

implementation_proposals: Dedicated daphne-server Protobuf/ZeroMQ PUB/SUB/TCP publication endpoint feeding the ZMQ client on the SC bridge server and its OPC UA bridge; schema and port require assignment and implementation qualification.

LCM control service has an OPC UA adapter in SC infrastructure; configuration/control request-response and published monitoring are requirements. LCM native control protocol details remain to be specified.

Ops arbitration: SC completes the handshake with Operations and publishes detector availability only after detector health and Ops authorization are confirmed. This allocation is proposed; handshake ownership remains to be agreed. No definite DAQ-to-Ops handshake is required by the revised text.
source_notes: R2 specifies a dedicated 1 GbE SFP CCM link per LCM and cathode PoF power. The four-group responsibility assignment follows the author instruction of 2026-09-17. No implemented calibration/PoF native protocol or DPS connection is asserted.
